newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian oil lifting supervisors threaten strike.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian oil lifting supervisors threaten strike.

text.p: Workers at Nigeria's petroleum department who supervise crude oil liftings said on Monday they would stop work from December 25 if salary arrears are not met.

"The oil workers told the (oil) minister that their demands must be met before Christmas day or they will go on strike," Ali Ciroma, sole administrator of the National Union of Petroleum and Natural Gas Workers (NUPENG) told Reuters.
The workers first served a similar threat last month which expired on Sunday but shelved it after they met oil minister Dan Etete on Saturday.
Ciroma said Etete told them that they should be patient as the government had not yet released the funds to pay them.
The workers are owed two months salary, a common thing in Nigeria but rare in the oil industry, the nation's economic engine.
"Union representatives and the minister will head to (the capital) Abuja tomorrow to meet government officials on the issue of the salary arrears," Ciroma said.
A spokeswoman for the Department of Petroleum Resources (DPR), which employs the aggrieved workers, said she hoped the strike would be avoided.
"We hope the minister solves the payment issue because knowing fully well our role in the oil industry we don't pray for the strike option," she said.
The last strike oil sector strike was in 1994 when it was crippled for two months by industrial action to protest against the arrest of presidential claimant Moshood Abiola.
